description: Add or remove FISH functions called at a point in the cycle sequence or when an event fires (entity creation/deletion, contact model events, solve start/end).

python_sdk_alternative.workaround: For a cycle position: itasca.set_callback('fn', position) registers a Python function from __main__, itasca.remove_callback('fn', position) removes it. The event-name form is not verified: set_callback('fn', 'solve_complete') followed by a cycle crashed PFC3D 9.8.54.

keywords.name: add
keywords.description: Register the FISH function sym: at position f of the cycle sequence (called every step), or when the event s fires. Entity creation/deletion events pass a pointer to the entity as the first argument and contact model events pass model-defined arguments, provided sym takes arguments.

keywords.name: remove
keywords.description: Remove one registration of sym: the first at position f, or the first for event s; with neither, sym is removed wherever it is found. For event registrations (bond_break on PFC 6.0 / 7.0 / 9.8) the bare form leaves the registration in place: name the event. 'fish list callbacks' shows what is registered.

examples: fish callback add servo -1.0 interval 10 process mechanical
fish callback add on_done event solve_complete
notes: 'fish callback add <sym> event ?' prints the event names this engine accepts and registers nothing.

Write event names in full: an unambiguous prefix is accepted, so 'struct_internal' (a 7.0 name) silently registers on struct_internal_complete. solve_master/solve_slave are rejected; use solve_leader/solve_follower.
interval, interval-time and process follow a cycle position only. After 'event <s>' they raise 'Unused extra parameter', but the callback has already been registered: remove it before retrying.
Some cycle positions are reserved for the engine's own callbacks ('Cannot add a fish call at a reserved location', e.g. 45.0 in PFC 9.8).
Verified on PFC3D 9.8.54 (2026-10-29): add/remove grammar, process values, the event names and the notes above.
